text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — kv-prefetch leak detected. Continuous-batching queues increasing rapidly for mixed-model traffic (Mistral + Qwen). Elevated tail latency and gradual error rise. Alert: https://alerts.internal/redwood/INC-5231

liz-oncall: ack — picking this up, paging SRE and runtime. grabbing pager.

mike-sre: looking at nodes; KV key-count per-shard jumped from ~40k -> ~420k in ~4m on shard gpu-12. 95p latency on generate endpoint up from 320ms -> 2.4s. error rate +0.8% mainly 504s.

neha-eng: timeline? did any prefetch rollout or config change hit earlier? I see a prefetch tuning job rolled at 2234564200 (safe rollouts service) — could be related.

alex-runtime: initial hypothesis: prefetch combinator created duplicate KV entries for mixed instruction+gqa sequences; continuous batching kept appending new prefixes (cache keys not deduping by model variant).

carmen-support: customers flagged: prod-tenant-42 and prod-tenant-88 seeing higher latencies and some timeouts. CS notified both and opened tickets.

mike-sre: quick mitigation options: 1) disable prefetch globally (big perf hit), 2) disable prefetch for GQA-tagged models only, 3) throttle continuous-batching max batch size and max outstanding batches. leaning to option 2 + 3 to reduce customer impact.

neha-eng: agree — apply selective disable first. patch config map:

```
# patch to disable prefetch for gqa/mqa models
prefetch:
  enabled_by_default: true
  disabled_model_tags:
    - gqa
    - mqa
```

kubectl apply -f runtime-prefetch-patch.yml -n redwood-runtime

```

ops-bot: Deploy started by neha-eng — job id 78921 — canary on 2 nodes. logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/78921

mike-sre: canary metrics: KV growth on canary nodes flattened within 30s. tail p95 dropped to ~620ms after 90s. errors trending down. rolling to remaining nodes now.

alex-runtime: also pushed a hotfix to cap per-key KV entries to 5k and added LRU eviction for stale prefixes — config snippet:

```
kv:
  per_key_limit: 5000
  eviction_policy: lru
continuous_batching:
  max_outstanding: 6
  max_batch_size: 32
```

mike-sre: rolling hotfix across runtime pool. watching for regressions.

carmen-support: prod-tenant-42 reports latency improving after 2m, timeouts gone. CS will keep monitoring and notify customers when fully stable. :thumbsup:

neha-eng: temp routing change applied to send critical customers through qwen-small fallback for high-latency requests to reduce end-user impact. routing rule id: route-3321.

liz-oncall: summary for handoff:
- Incident: KV-prefetch leak causing KV growth + cont-batching perf cliff for mixed Mistral/Qwen workloads
- Mitigations applied: disabled prefetch for GQA/MQA tags, capped per-key KV to 5k, lowered continuous-batching concurrency + canary rollout, temporary customer routing to qwen-small
- Current status: mitigated and rolling; metrics stable on canaries, cluster-wide rollout 60% complete as of last check
- Customer impact: degraded p95 and some 504s for a small subset of tenants; CS notified and customers being followed up
- Next steps: postmortem, add unit/regression tests for prefetch dedupe across variants, verify long-term memory usage, monitor for reappearance for 6h

mike-sre: monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/runtime/kv-prefetch — alerts suppressed for now but still notifying p95>1s.

james-eng: assigning follow-up tasks:
- alex-runtime -> create repro harness for mixed-instruction+gqa sequences and validate fix (INF-4312)
- neha-eng -> add canary gating to prefetch rollouts and update runbook (INF-4313)
- mike-sre -> correlate which customers hit fallback routing and validate SLA impacts (INF-4314)

ops-bot: Created tickets INF-4312, INF-4313, INF-4314 and linked to this thread.

liz-oncall: handing off to neha-eng for next 2h watch window. neha — you're primary. i'll remain reachable for escalation. leaving pager. :pray:

neha-eng: taking over, ack. will monitor for next 2h and then hand to oncall rotation. will update when clear.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Updating incident dashboard and scheduling follow-up postmortem. :white_check_mark:
